highlights.title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI
highlights.summary: Indian workers are being paid to film themselves at work and the footage is used to train AI.
body: Mohammed Ashim has been cutting hair and trimming beards for four years in Bengaluru.
But recently the 22-year old has been strapping a camera to his head to record his work.
The camera only records his hands and fingers - his client's faces are blurred out.

"The routine is simple, but you have to be disciplined about how you move. The operations team taught me that my hands always have to stay cleanly inside the frame, the lighting has to be sharp, and I can't tilt my head too abruptly while working."

highlights.title: Q&A: How AI came to model the “messy” human mind
highlights.summary: Assistant Professor Benjamin Lindquist studies how engineers deliberately injected randomness into early AI, giving rise to deep-learning models that sometimes hallucinate.
body: Generative artificial intelligence models are rooted in ideas of mid-20th century engineers who thought some amount of irrationality was essential for a machine that could think like a human, contends Benjamin Lindquist, an assistant professor in the MIT History Section, who holds an MIT Schwarzman College of Computing shared position with the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) and is a principal investigator in the Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems.

To mimic creative thinking, these AI pioneers intentionally injected randomness into algorithms designed to deterministically solve problems, Lindquist writes in a new paper that appears in the journal Past and Present. In the paper, he traces the origins of AI hallucinations back to this early research and suggests there will be inevitable tradeoffs between creativity and predictability when trying to build machines that mimic human behavior. MIT News spoke with Lindquist about these ideas.
Q: Why did early computer engineers believe they needed to inject randomness and irrationality into AI systems designed for logic and calculation?

highlights.title: 'Out of control' - Verstappen criticises 'unacceptable' track surface
highlights.summary: Max Verstappen revealed concerns over the state of his spine as he unleashed a scathing criticism of the "out of control" bumpy track surface at Circuit of The Americas.
body: The four-time world champion arrives in Austin for Sunday's United States Grand Prix after claiming his first two victories of the season in back-to-back races.
Speaking to the media on Thursday, Verstappen was unexpectedly passionate over the state of the circuit, which is generally considered as one of the most popular among the drivers on the F1 calendar.
"You can also see the track conditions. From what I saw in the WEC [World Endurance Championship], the circuit was extremely bumpy," Verstappen said.

"I'm not really looking forward to that to be honest, for your spine. I was joking about that in the last race but it's not really a joke to be honest because we mentioned this already for years that it's actually getting a bit out of control.

body: Despite the name, Avatar: Seven Havens has focused almost exclusively on Ellora, the Haven of Wind and Sand situated somewhere in the desert expanses of the post-apocalyptic world. The first six episodes established that the remote Havens are, for the most part, disconnected from one another. In Ellora, it’s even illegal to contact another Haven without permission from the council.
Her plea culminates in a two-part summit across episodes 8 and 9. That’s right: We finally meet survivors from other parts of the world.

The summit is initially intended to address the crisis consuming Ellora. Not only are Bender birth rates on the decline, but the fear-based Affliction is spreading thanks to the red Anomaly crystals growing beneath the city. The Bending Brigade can barely maintain order. But the visiting delegations reveal that some of Ellora’s problems are common. Benders are becoming scarce throughout the world, other Havens are struggling to produce enough food, and everyone seems to need resources their neighbors possess.

highlights.title: Supercell hit by cyberattack, but says no player data was affected
highlights.summary: The Clash of Clans developer says it was the target of multiple attacks last week and has notified police and regulators.
body: Supercell has confirmed that an unauthorised party has accessed a platform Supercell used to host company meetings and presentations.

In an announcement on October 21, the Clash of Clans developer said it was targeted by multiple cyberattacks last week, one of which caused the incident. Based on its investigations so far, Supercell believes no player data was affected.

It says it blocked further access, took the service offline and began investigating the platform and its security experts. It has since filed a police report, submitted a notification under the EU Cyber Resilience Act, and notified the Data Protection Ombudsman, but said that because the investigation is ongoing, it cannot share further details at this time.

The videos include current and former employees, as well as some guests and partners who took part in internal events. They may contain people’s names, images and voices, and the names and email addresses of the platform’s users were also accessed.

highlights.title: OpenAI and Poland’s NASK partner to advance AI safety and security
highlights.summary: OpenAI and Poland’s NASK are partnering on AI safety, security, and technical research to strengthen safeguards and support a more resilient digital ecosystem.
body: OpenAI and Poland’s NASK National Research Institute have signed an agreement to explore collaboration on AI safety, security and technical research. The partnership will bring together expertise from both organizations to better understand emerging risks, strengthen safeguards, and explore how advanced AI can contribute to a more secure and resilient digital ecosystem.

As AI systems become more capable, international collaboration between developers and public research institutions will be essential to understanding their risks and building stronger safeguards. OpenAI’s existing work with the US Center for Advancing Standards and Innovation for Super Intelligence (CAISSI), UK AI Security Institute (AISI) and other public research institutions around the world has already helped strengthen safeguards, identify and fix security vulnerabilities in AI agents, and advance frontier AI safety.

highlights.summary: Lando Norris believes Kimi Antonelli has done an "incredible job" and performed "two levels above" Mercedes team-mate George Russell this season, in form which has taken the Italian to the brink of a record-breaking world championship triumph.
body: Antonelli looks all but assured to succeed Norris as F1's reigning world champion this year thanks to the 102-point lead he holds at the top of the standings with six races left.

The 20-year-old could become the sport's youngest-ever champion as early as this Sunday's United States Grand Prix if he wins the race and nearest challengers Russell and Lewis Hamilton do not score sufficient points to stay in mathematical contention.
And Norris, who claimed his own maiden crown with McLaren last year, has spoken glowingly about Antonelli's second season of F1 up against the "very good" Russell.
"I think it's very impressive what he's been able to do," said Norris.

highlights.title: 5 'Solo Leveling' Characters Who Deserved So Much Better
highlights.summary: Jin-woo starts out as a weak E-Rank hunter trapped in a seemingly endless struggle to survive. Before long, though, he becomes an unstoppable force. His progression feels steady and earned, and his efforts to uncover the source of his abilities take him through a series of unforgettable fights.
body: Solo Leveling is the ultimate power fantasy. Based on Chugong’s web novel, which was later adapted into an acclaimed webtoon, the story takes place in a world where hunters wield supernatural abilities to battle dangerous beasts and protect humanity from extinction. Hunters are ranked by strength, but a video game-like interface known as the System lets our protagonist, Sung Jin-woo, climb the ranks and grow stronger at an astonishing pace.

It’s easy to see why Solo Leveling has become so popular. The series is an ever-escalating power fantasy that stays flashy and fun, even when it puts spectacle ahead of depth. That doesn’t make the story any less enjoyable. When its protagonist is relatable and easy to root for, straightforward world-building and likable supporting characters can be more than enough — especially in an anime elevated by impressive animation.

highlights.title: ‘A form of anti-status status’ – how much would you pay for a plain tote bag?
highlights.summary: The ubiquitous carrier has been given a four-figure makeover. But why has an everyday bag associated with running errands and US supermarkets become so aspirational? • Don’t get Fashion Statement delivered to your inbox? Sign up here.
body: I f you were in the blessed position of having £500 to spend on a bag, what would you look for? Would it be made of cotton? A nice light shade bound to sully quickly, like “paper white” or ecru? Would you want something that looks a lot like those ubiquitous totes sold by a certain US supermarket chain for a couple of dollars?

No, thought not. But there are plenty of options if you do. Phoebe Philo, former Celine designer and quiet luxury pioneer, offers a white canvas shopper, made entirely from cotton except for the silver brass hardware of its internal zipped pocket, for £450. Luxury Swedish brand Toteme’s “effortless tote bag” is made from organic cotton canvas and is available in dark brown, red or classic ecru. It goes for £510. Tom Ford’s version, at £1,600, differentiates itself a little, with a body made exclusively of cotton canvas but trims and handles from calfskin. Prada’s, which features leather details and metal hardware, could be yours for over £2,000.

The new AI model builds on Canva’s big push into AI. In April, Canva launched new prompt-based editing capabilities that allow you to create or make changes to a design by describing it. The design tool also brought layers to AI-generated images, which let you make changes to part of an image while leaving the rest untouched.

Canva says it trained Craft on “millions of human-made templates” from the platform’s content library, which includes things like social media posts, presentations, infographics, and menus. The model is currently ranked fourth on Design Arena’s leaderboard for the best AI image generation models, a crowdsourced benchmark for AI designs. highlights.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 review – a thrilling airport novel of a game
highlights.summary: Activision; PC, PS5, Switch 2, Xbox From parkour over Manhattan rooftops and car chases in Paris to the climactic battle at a North Korean air base, the developers have thrown absolutely everything at the game.
body: A nd so we return perhaps one final time to Call of Duty’s Modern Warfare strand, with stories, “ripped from the newspaper headlines”, featuring shady terror organisations, nefarious rogue states and the brutally capable, monosyllabic war fighters who stand between us and Armageddon. Last year’s Black Ops 7 instalment was a sales disappointment for Activision, and that has no doubt put extra pressure on Infinity Ward, the studio leading Modern Warfare 4 development. Fortunately, this developer – like series heroes Price, Gaz and Ghost – seems to thrive on pressure.

As you may have read, this year’s campaign is based around a fictitious North Korean ruling family that has seized an opportunity to invade its southern neighbour. Amid the chaos, a small group of Korean and American marines must help lead the fightback, while in the shadows, SAS hard man John Price makes an unlikely new comrade in his own morally ambiguous quest to put the world to rights. Mads Mikkelsen pops up as evil mastermind The Archer, but like Kiernan Shipka in Black Ops 7 he’s rather wasted, with very little screen time.

body: This time around they sit bottom of the pile with four points from seven games. Things were always going to be tough with the additional load of European football to contend with, something Sunderland haven't experienced in over 50 years.
The performance at Bournemouth on Sunday, fresh from an away Europa league clash in Portugal, was littered with mistakes and individual errors.

It led to defender Nordi Mukiele suggesting post-match that the team had become "arrogant". That felt like the wrong choice of words from the Frenchman. I don't detect that mindset, but without doubt the schedule, both mentally and physically, is having an effect.
There was a feeling from within the club that those exertions of European football would be challenging this season, and that is playing out in the results.

highlights.title: 27 Years Later, Linus' Final 'Peanuts' Quote Is a Brilliant Comic Strip Callback
highlights.summary: Charles Schulz's Peanuts, for whatever reason, has one of the more dedicated fan communities on the internet. The Peanuts Fandom wiki is an invaluable resource for anything you might want to know about the strip, from obscure characters to running jokes to the gang’s unofficial cameo appearances in…
body: Somewhat more depressingly, the wiki features a rundown of the daily Peanuts strip that includes all of its various unofficial finales. As you flip through the last couple of months' worth of published Peanuts strips, you encounter footnotes about everything in the strip that’s now over.

By the end of January 2000, almost every character, interaction, catchphrase, and recurring scenario in Peanuts has appeared for the last time: the football gag (Oct. 24, 1999), the Great Pumpkin (Halloween 1999), Snoopy's weird cousin Spike (Dec. 21, 1999), Lucy Van Pelt (Dec. 13, 1999), etc. In most of those cases, Schulz hadn't been aware he was drawing a sendoff. He'd just been going about his usual business until he was suddenly forced into medical retirement.

As a result, Peanuts has no official final chapter besides Schulz's farewell note on Feb. 13, 2000. There are a couple of strips that feel like they've got some degree of subtext regarding Schulz's failing health, like Nov. 1, 1999 ("You're the last one... did you turn out the light?”) or Peppermint Patty's last appearance, but that's primarily an exercise left for the reader.

highlights.title: Benjamina Ebuehi’s recipe for chocolate and pumpkin spice choux buns | The sweet spot
highlights.summary: Whip winter squash puree into a creamy filling and pipe direct into the heart of a cracking seasonal pudding. At this time of year, I aim to get as much pumpkin as I can into my meals, including desserts.
body: Briefly mix the butter and sugar for the craquelin in a small bowl, until smooth and well combined, then work in the flour and cocoa powder to make a thick paste. Spread this evenly over a sheet of baking paper, top with a second sheet, then roll out to about 2-3mm thick and pop it in the freezer to firm up.

Meanwhile, make the choux. Put the milk, butter and 50ml water in a saucepan and heat until steaming and the butter has melted. Off the heat, add the flour, sugar and salt, and stir quickly to bring the dough together. Return to the heat, cook, stirring, for one or two minutes, then transfer to a clean bowl and leave to cool for a few minutes.

Meanwhile, whisk the eggs in a jug, then bit by bit work some into the dough, mixing until it’s all incorporated before adding more. The dough will look lumpy at first, but it will come together. Continue mixing in the eggs (you may not need all of them) until the mixture is glossy, falls easily, and leaves a V shape hanging when lifted with a spoon. Transfer to a piping bag, snip off 2½cm from the end and pipe 12 blobs of the choux dough on to a lined tray.

Under the new policies, every listing must include “at least one unedited photo of the actual item against a real background,” and all photos must “accurately represent the item a buyer will receive.” The photos that aren’t the first one can be edited with software or AI-powered tools, as long as “the final result remains an accurate representation of the physical product.” The company shared a few examples to demonstrate the type of misleading images that are prohibited, including the cat stuffed animal at the top of this post.

While uploading images for a listing, if Etsy detects that any may be AI-generated, the platform will show a pop-up where you can note if an image was made with AI or not, as shown in a video. If a buyer reports that what they receive is “materially different” from a listing, a seller may be responsible for a refund.
points: Etsy is announcing stricter rules about how AI can be used in listings to reduce the volume of AI slop on the platform.

highlights.title: Designing an AI serving harness built to last
highlights.summary: The next competitive advantage in enterprise AI has less to do with which model you choose than with what you build around it. That’s an important shift. For the past several years, much of the AI conversation has centered on model capability: bigger models, better reasoning, larger context…
body: Increasingly, the answer depends on the serving harness—the engineering system surrounding the model, including the architecture, memory management, scheduling, and optimization decisions that determine how efficiently model intelligence becomes a production capability.
For technical executives, that changes where AI investment should go—and what they should demand from the architecture supporting it.
There is no universally “best” model or AI architecture. There is only the right solution for the business problem.

A customer-facing assistant optimized for fast responses has fundamentally different requirements from a document-processing pipeline that can run overnight. An internal knowledge application and a high-volume customer service platform may use the same foundation model but require very different serving architectures.
points: The next competitive advantage in enterprise AI has less to do with which model you choose than with what you build around it.

highlights.title: 25 Years Since Its Reveal, and People Still Search for iPods “Every Two Seconds” on eBay
highlights.summary: It’s October 23, 2001. Headline: “Apple Presents iPod”. It promised "1,000 songs in your pocket" and fundamentally sparked what turned Apple into the most valuable electronics brand in the world. Yet, a quarter of a century later, Apple’s official storefronts bear no trace of it.
body: iPod is still going strong in the secondhand market, however, at least according to the latest marketplace data from eBay. Nostalgia for the iconic device is clear, with someone searching for an "iPod" on eBay "every two seconds worldwide".
This renaissance aligns with a broader consumer revolution according to eBay, with 76% of consumers surveyed having shopped secondhand in the past year.

Or, perhaps, this could also represent more evidence for an even greater shift in the tech industry. Stop me if you’ve heard this one before, but everything is rather expensive right now, isn’t it? Groundbreaking, I know. So let’s narrow the scope a little further.

Streaming is front and center for a lot of consumers right now. Whether that’s Netflix and Disney+ for film and TV, or Spotify for music streaming. And there’s a monthly cost attached to instantly stream media; we all know this. But it’s a cost that continues to tick upward, without offering any greater value to the consumer.

highlights.title: Experience: I’ve climbed Mount Everest 20 times
highlights.summary: In 1996 doctors told me I wouldn’t walk again unaided, but in 2022 I took the record for the most Everest summits by a non-Sherpa. I grew up in Slough, Berkshire, in a bungalow beside a farm.
body: When I was 17, a school friend took me to a climbing wall where he was a regular. I loved the physicality of it and trying to work out where to put my hands and feet next. We would go there twice a week. In sixth form, we headed to the south coast in Dorset for my first real climbing outing. The waves were crashing and it felt scary and exhilarating. I thought it was magical.

We would go climbing there or in the Peak District whenever we could. After A-levels, we caught a bus to Chamonix, in the Alps, for five weeks of camping; we climbed Mont Blanc and made stupid mistakes like starting too late in the day. It was a huge learning curve, but it was fabulous.

I did a geology degree at the University of Leeds and joined the climbing club. I wanted to see the Himalayas, so organised a trip to Pakistan. That was a turning point. The climbing was wonderful, but it was the people I fell in love with.

highlights.title: Palmer Luckey Made a Genetically Modified Military Dog Startup
highlights.summary: Warhound came out of stealth on Wednesday with $200 million in funding and a mission to create “elite working dogs” equipped with "advanced body armor."
body: A new startup launched today with the definitely not terrifying mission of creating genetically enhanced dogs for the United States military, law enforcement, and emergency first responders.

Warhound is the brainchild of Anduril’s Palmer Luckey and Colossal Biosciences cofounder Ben Lamm. The startup has raised $200 million to “rebuild America’s domestic supply of elite working dogs” and reduce dependency on European dog breeders for military canines.

Lamm tells WIRED that Warhound is in the process of gene-editing its first batch of dogs. The startup has already collected blood samples from specific "top-performing” military, police, and first responder dogs in the United States, and its goal is to clone them. Breeds will be “mostly Belgian Malinois, some labs, and some shepherds,” he says. The company anticipates the first round of puppies to be born in early 2027.

highlights.title: This design software reimagines everyday objects as self-aware devices
highlights.summary: “X-Hinges” helps design and 3D print items like lamps and gloves with an interactive twist: automatically embedded sensors that perceive and adaptively respond to human contact.
body: Jiaji Li and lead author Xiang Chang, a TJU PhD student and visiting researcher at CSAIL, used X-Hinges to create many clever devices. For example, they made a glove that can teach a robot how to grasp blocks. It adjusts to the size of a user’s hands, then records how the joints in their fingers bend via sensors before rapidly relaying that information to a humanoid hand to mimic it. The glove could be useful in factories or homes, where a robot often needs to learn new interactions quickly.

The researchers also produced a small, origami-style lamp using X-Hinges. It senses when a human pinches it closed and adjusts its brightness accordingly. When you turn on this adaptive, portable light source (sort of like a reading light), it looks like a piece of folded-up paper that sprouts into a lamp.

X-Hinges can even assemble devices that identify which objects have been placed on it. You could put a banana on top, for instance, and it’ll recognize the fruit almost immediately based on the tactile data it’s recorded using its sensors. This advanced physical awareness could be integrated into detection systems in places such as airports and grocery stores.

highlights.title: Anya Taylor-Joy’s breakout movie gave horror a different kind of female lead
highlights.summary: Anya Taylor-Joy has established herself as one of her era's most versatile actors. At 30, she's built a career across film and television, appearing in franchises like Super Mario and Mad Max, along with winning a Golden Globe for her role in The Queen’s Gambit.
body: The Witch follows a devout, isolated Puritan family in 1630s New England, a time when witches, myth, and folklore quietly stood at the root of most people’s everyday fears. Following their exile from the religious community due to a dispute with the church, a family of seven is forced to relocate to the outskirts of society, with the dark, unmapped woods mere feet away.

The film is steeped in its historical setting, and its characters speak a dense form of archaic English, with religion at the very center of their lives. That can be a tough watch for modern viewers, but The Witch ultimately tells a simple story about a family hitting its breaking point.

With no animals left to hunt and their crops rotting, William (Ralph Ineson) and his wife Katherine (Kate Dickie) are desperate. They spend their days bitterly arguing in their cramped home and blaming each other for everything that goes wrong. Their younger kids absorb the tension (and perhaps Black Phillip's devilish whispers), acting out in ways that make everyone's lives more difficult. Things boil over when the family’s newborn, Samuel, disappears under the watch of their eldest daughter, Thomasin (Anya Taylor-Joy).

highlights.summary: Meta has tweaked its business terms to remove language suggesting that it could freely train its AI models on news sites, like The Verge - but legal experts say these changes aren't enough to address their concerns.
body: Meta’s new business terms could still help it justify training AI on scraped sites.

Initially, Meta’s new terms for business accounts appeared to give the company permission to train its AI on news sites. The terms, which go into effect October 30th, stated that Meta “may use any content” from the websites associated with a business account to “develop, research” and “train” Meta’s products. At the time, legal experts told Nieman Lab that this could allow Meta “to argue its commercial terms supersede other blocking instructions,” such as the robots.txt file that has historically told scrapers (including search engines like Google) what they are allowed to crawl.

highlights.title: Asif Kapadia on Bringing the ‘Profound’ ‘7 Up’ Documentary Series to a Close After More Than 60 Years: ‘It’s a Dream Job’
highlights.summary: From a charismatic Formula 1 racing legend to a brilliant but flawed soccer god to a troubled, tragic singer, Academy Award-winning docmaker Asif Kapadia has made a career out of telling the stories of larger-than-life figures.
body: The “Up” series of films launched in 1964 with “7 Up,” capturing the lives of 10 boys and four girls in England all aged seven at the time. Cameras then revisited the group every seven years to chart their journey from childhood to teenagers, to adulthood, through careers, marriage, divorce, parenting, bereavement and more.
The longest-running documentary series ever made, it’s been broadcast in 157 countries, including the U.S., Canada, Japan, China, Australia and France.

All but the first in the series were directed by Michael Apted, who passed away in 2021. Kapadia was handed the baton to direct the final installment, saying he “felt very honored and privileged to have a chance to be a part of it.”
“It was like finishing off something someone had started — just closing the circle,” he said. “It’s a dream job.”
